newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West electricity prices mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West electricity prices mostly higher.

text.p: U.S. Midwestern spot wholesale electricity prices were mostly higher Monday, drawing some psychological strength from higher spot natural gas prices, industry sources said.

Prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) climbed in tandem with higher Texas electricity prices, which in turn had drawn strength from increases in spot natural gas prices, the brokers and marketers said.
On-peak SPP power for Tuesday delivery was said to be talked near $26.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from quotes late last week for Monday delivery at $18.50-20.00.
Off-peak prices in SPP were reported to be holding steady however in the $12.00-14.00 area, the sources said.
Peak, non-firm power for Tuesday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) region was quoted at $18.00-21.00 from a Monday delivery range of $16.00-17.00, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was said to be steady at $10.00-11.50 per megawatt hour (MWh).

In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), non-firm peak power was again talked close to MAPP prices, with Tuesday power pegged at $18.50-20.75 from a Monday range of $16.00-17.00 per MWh, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next day MAIN power was pegged steady at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.
In the East Central Area Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak, non-firm electricity prices for Tuesday were assessed at $16.50-20.00 from a Monday delivery range of $18.00-20.00.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was talked steady in the $12.50-14.00 area, the sources said.
November ECAR prices held steady at $17.00-17.40, while December was pegged steady at $18.70-19.10. Some July/August 1997 power was talked at $25.55 per MWh, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
